task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L
play-type possession records derived from play-by-play
substitution rotation intervals and lineup spells
methodological_questions: Does offensive reorganization relative to L predict the change in PPP after a player absence?
Is the reorganization measure reliable and independent of the outcome it is meant to predict?
How many absence spells are needed to detect a practically relevant rho, and does the data reach that?
Are absence-spell selection, regression to the mean, and outcome-derived play-type labels controlled?
Do the retrieved small-sample and gating artifacts recur in this design?

historical_evidence.finding: Absence validation study. Real absences moved the association structure (V1). [prior work]: Gate G2 21/23 above null median; V1(a) 16/23 above own-null p95, binomial p=2.67e-16; V1(b) +0.142, CI [+0.103, +0.187]. [prior work] and [prior work]: V2a (simulation predicts magnitude) rho=+0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667], FAIL; V2b partial rho=+0.253, p=0.115, CI [-0.262, +0.615], FAIL. Limited by small sample.

Live trigger timing study (early vs late detection). [prior work]: tier Spearman rho -0.2066, p=1e-06, n=557; BEST-AVOID gap early 0.701 vs late 0.415. [prior work]: 101 triggers, Spearman tier vs ROG PPP rho=-0.0457, p=0.456, n=268; MW BEST vs AVOID p=0.074, not confirmed at 0.05. [prior work]: 228 triggers, rho=-0.2066, p=1e-06, n=557; MW p=0.0. Auto-confidence low (0.26).

Player routing V4 vs V5 direct scoring. 8 divergences, 0 scoreable, 8 unscored because the player was missing from [source] database; V5 mostly routed to 'team' rather than a player. Failure type A_unanswerable; risks DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER recorded.

Routing prior vs H2H posterior gate diagnostic. [prior work] and [prior work]: the mean PPP delta for lead-vs-default was +1.26 at n>=5 and +1.13 at n>=15, but low-n leaders were 1-shot role players with 2-3 PPP on 5-7 possessions, so the apparent [source] was small-sample inflation.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing observed PPP between divergent player-routing choices (V4 vs V5) on a small set of divergences
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: 0 of 8 divergences were scoreable because players were missing from [source] database, and V5 mostly routed to 'team'. Sample too small ([prior work]).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading a PPP-delta [source] from low-count player-level possession samples (n>=5 to n>=15 gates)
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: the apparent +1.13 PPP [source] was produced by small-sample distortion (e.g. n=6, PPP=3.00).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Simulation-based prediction of the magnitude of association change after real absences (V2a/V2b)
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable with limit [prior work]. Both V2 checks failed with CIs spanning zero, though the structural V1 check was confirmed.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project studies on related absence and routing questions exist, and small-sample and gating artifacts have already appeared in this project's per-player PPP work.

Real absences were reported to move an association structure in one earlier family ([prior work], V1 confirmed), which is indirect support that absence matters for the structure this question targets.
Player-level PPP estimates with 5-15 possessions are unreliable in these records ([prior work]).
Graph-database coverage gaps can make player-level scoring impossible (SF-[prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: None of the retrieved records tests whether offensive reorganization relative to L predicts the change in PPP. Their research questions concern trigger timing, absence validation, and routing.
No record reports a reorganization measure, an L definition, or a reorganization-to-PPP-change effect size.
The retrieved records are truncated ('read_family for the full text'); I did not read the full text of any record.
No record shows that the 2022-26 data reach the power needed for a spell-level rho.
The meaning of 'n=148, mde rho' in the unit description is unclear and is not resolved by [prior work].
own_inferences: The question as posed is not a restatement of any retrieved study, so prior work does not answer it.
The closest evidence ([prior work]) suggests absence effects on association structure are detectable at the structural level, but magnitude predictions were not reliable at that sample size.
With about 148 spells, a modest rho (around 0.2-0.3) would be near the [source] of detectability, so a null result would be weakly informative.
Reorganization measured from the same play-type records that carry points risks outcome-derived labels, which could create an artificial association with PPP change.
uncertainties: The definition of L and of 'offensive reorganization' is not provided in the task. The glossary was not consulted.
The meaning of 'n=986' versus '148 spells' and whether they are independent units is unclear.
The MDE for rho is not stated numerically.
How many absence spells fall in each season and playoff segment is unknown.
The 2025-26 regular season and playoffs are partial at the date of the question, which could cause outcome drift or incomplete data.
Retrieved records were truncated, so details of their controls and gates are unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: Before retrieval, the question looked answerable with 148 absence spells and a play-type dataset. The retrieved records changed the decision in two ways. [prior work] shows that low-count PPP differences produce artifacts, which makes spell-level PPP-change estimates risky. [prior work] and SF-[prior work] show that absence-based magnitude predictions and player-level comparisons failed or were untestable at this scale. Together these moved the decision from proceed toward do_not_proceed as posed. [prior work] do not directly test the question, so they are evidence about risk, not an answer.

blocking_constraints.text: About 148 absence spells may give too little power for a rho near 0.2-0.3; the MDE is unstated and earlier small-sample families failed or were artifacts.
Reorganization measured from play-type records that include points can mechanically correlate with PPP change.
Per-player and per-spell possession counts may be too few for stable PPP and reorganization estimates.
The reorganization measure relative to L has no recorded reliability assessment.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests reorganization relative to L predicting PPP change. [prior work] is the nearest, studying whether absences move association structure; its structural check was confirmed, but its magnitude predictions were not. [prior work] (trigger timing), SF-[prior work] (routing, untestable), and [prior work] (routing gate, artifact) concern other questions. They are relevant mainly as evidence of small-sample and labelling risks.

risks.text: 148 spells with an unstated MDE; earlier small-n families produced artifacts ([prior work]) or failed magnitude checks ([prior work]).
Low possession counts per spell or per player, as in [prior work], may make reorganization and PPP estimates unstable.
Reorganization relative to L is not defined in the task and has no reliability evidence.
Absence spells are selected at extreme or unusual states, so regression to the mean could create a spurious reorganization-PPP link.
Play-type records carry points, so reorganization labels may be derived from the outcome.
If reorganization uses data from the same possessions or after the absence, it may leak the outcome.
Opponent quality, lineup, pace, and injury context could drive both reorganization and PPP change.
Pooling 2022-23 to 2025-26 and partial 2025-26 data mixes eras and rule or roster changes.
Several reorganization definitions, windows, and L choices would inflate false positives.
Graph coverage gaps (SF-[prior work]) could silently drop players or spells from scoring.
If most absences show little reorganization, the usable spell count may be far below 148.
Substitution intervals and starter attribution may mislabel which player was absent.
Without a placebo or shuffled-absence check, the reorganization signal cannot be separated from structure in the data.

design.estimand: Within-spell association (Spearman and partial) between the offensive reorganization measure relative to L and the change in PPP after a player absence, as defined in a pre-registered L and reorganization definition. This is not yet defined in the task.
design.unit: Absence spell (one player absence within one team and season segment), with the reorganization measure computed only from possessions before the absence window.
design.sample: All spells from 2022-23 to 2024-25 (regular season and playoffs) plus completed 2025-26 segments only. Partial 2025-26 data is excluded. Spells need a minimum possession count set in advance; spells below it are excluded and the exclusion is reported.
design.power: Compute the MDE for rho at alpha=0.05 with the actual spell count after the possession threshold. Stop and report as untestable if the MDE exceeds a pre-set practical threshold (suggested rho around 0.25). Do not run the test if power is inadequate.
design.controls: Reorganization computed from pre-absence possessions only, to avoid leakage. Use placebo absences (same players in non-absence windows) as negative controls. Adjust for opponent strength, pace, lineup, and season. Use outcome-independent reorganization labels, with points excluded from the labelling step. Check regression to the mean by comparing against matched-absence controls.
design.falsification: Reject the hypothesis if the pre-registered partial rho is not positive with its lower CI bound above zero, or if the placebo spells show a comparable association. Also treat as failed if a shuffled-absence check reproduces the effect.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register a single primary reorganization definition and window. Report alternatives as exploratory with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the pre-registered primary partial rho is positive, its 95% CI excludes zero, it exceeds the placebo association, and it survives the outcome-leakage and regression-to-the-mean checks. Otherwise report as uncertain, or as an artifact if the checks reproduce the effect. Report power for a null outcome.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 through 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season after 2026-04-13 and 2025-26 playoffs after 2026-06-21. Record the snapshot date and do not use partial data.
